question: Who sent the most emails mentioning EnronOnline in 2001?

steps.text:
Plan: (1) count emails mentioning "EnronOnline" in 2001 by sender; (2) check variants ("Enron Online", "EOL"); (3) read what the top sender wrote to see why.

Counting 2001 emails mentioning EnronOnline by sender, to find the top writer.

I'm checking the question about EnronOnline, where Tana Jones has the highest count at 77. I want to see whether those counts only include emails she sent, since she might also be using more than one address. I'll pull a sample of her emails and look at the find_person results.
Tana Jones leads on the exact term. I'll check her other addresses and read what she wrote.

steps.summary: 10 results, 10 of them people's own mail

answer:
Tana Jones sent the most 2001 emails that mention "EnronOnline". The `mail_counts` tool shows 77 from her tana.jones@enron.com address, out of 1,412 matching emails in 2001.

- **Runners-up:** Adam Johnson is not the one I cite here, but the same count has him second with 57. Justin Rostant had 48, Matt Motsinger 45 and M. Schmidt 42.
- **Her other addresses:** Her other addresses, such as b.jones@enron.com, sent very little mail, so they don't change the ranking. She sent 4,152 emails from tana.jones@enron.com overall.
- **Other spellings:** I also counted the spelling "Enron Online" with a space. Michelle Lokay led that count with 44, and Tana Jones had only 4. Combining the two spellings could in principle change the order. I only checked the top 15 senders for each, so I can't rule out a different overall leader.
- **What she wrote:** Her mail is about approving counterparties to trade on EnronOnline.
  - On 2001-04-26 she sent an "EOL Country Approval List", a "cheat sheet" for approving non-US counterparties that come in through EnronOnline via Houston Credit.
  - On 2001-04-17 she wrote that a long-standing counterparty could not be approved on EnronOnline because it could not be set up in GCP.

The sources are the senders' own emails, not forwarded press.

citations.cited_text:
Subject: Re: Draft Responses to FERC Staff
From: louise.kitchen@enron.com
Date: 2001-06-25

As we discussed, attached is my "Cheat Sheet" which I use to guide me when 
approving non-US counterparties that come in through EnronOnline via Houston 
Credit.  London Legal and I try to coordinate our responses but I cannot 
speak for them and the standards they may apply to approving counterparties 
to trade online.  They also frequently deal with different countries than 
us.  You may want to speak to Justin Boyd.  Generally, with respect to most 
physical trading, except power trading, there are no legal restrictions to 
trading.  Most of the restrictions in this list are with respect to financial 
products.  Physical bandwidth has generally not done much legal due diligence 
outside of the US and the UK and bandwidth is therefore not open to non US 
and UK counterparties.

We have another long standing counterparty we cannot get approved on 
EnronOnline because we cannot get the counterparty set up in GCP.  The 
Counterparty sent in a Password Application styled:  Koch Industries, Inc., 
acting through its Koch Hydrocarbon Company Division.  (Which also happens to 
be the same styling on the Master Swap Agreement we have in place with this 
Counterparty.)
